record.Description: This recall involves the Kakgold 4WD stunt vehicles with a remote-control containing button cell and lithium-ion batteries. The toy car has a lime green and blue body, a black chassis and four black wheels with lime green trim and diagonal rollers. The vehicle body features checkered patterns, an “X” design and the words “PRO” and “RACING.” A white hang tag attached to the vehicle body displays “Do Not Twist the Shaft” in red lettering and illustrations marked with red crosses.
record.Title: Kakgold Recalls 4WD Remote-Controlled Car Toys Due to Risk of Serious Injury or Death from Battery Ingestion; Violate Mandatory Standard for Toys

Hazards.Name: The recalled remote-controlled cars violate the mandatory standard for toys because they contain button cell and lithium-ion batteries in the remote control that can be easily accessed by children, posing a deadly ingestion hazard to children. When button cell or coin batteries are swallowed, the ingested batteries can cause serious injuries, internal chemical burns and death

Remedies.Name:
Consumers should stop using the remote-controlled car toys immediately and contact Kakgold for information on how to receive a full refund. Consumers will be asked to write “RECALLED” on the product and email a photograph showing the product being properly disposed of in the trash to kakrecall@outlook.com.

Note: Button cell batteries are hazardous. Batteries should be disposed of or recycled by following local hazardous waste procedures.

ai.summary: Kakgold has recalled its 4WD stunt vehicle toys because children can easily access the button cell and lithium-ion batteries inside the remote control. Swallowing button cell batteries can lead to severe internal chemical burns or even death. Because of this hazard, the toys fail to meet mandatory safety standards.
ai.next_steps: Consumers should immediately stop using the toy vehicles and contact Kakgold by emailing kakrecall@outlook.com to receive a full refund. To get the refund, mark the toy with the word “RECALLED” and email a photo showing the item properly discarded in the trash. Button cell batteries must be recycled or disposed of according to your local hazardous waste procedures.
